expectations.text: Rewrite collapses enumerated ALWAYS/NEVER micro-rules into fewer principle-based instructions with stated reasons
expectations.evidence: Eight micro-rules become four principle paragraphs (plan proportional to task, risk-based confirmation, style with rationale, selective replies). Reasons are embedded, e.g., 'code that needs a comment per line usually needs a rewrite instead'. Change note: 'Collapsed eight absolutes into four principles with reasons.'

expectations.text: The 'explain your reasoning step by step in your response' instruction is removed or replaced (not kept as-is)
expectations.evidence: Replaced with 'lead with what you did or found and the one decision worth knowing about.' Change note: 'Deleted "explain your reasoning step by step" — reasoning models already reason internally; asking for a transcript just bloats responses.'

expectations.text: The contradiction between 'be concise' and 'extensive comments explaining each line' is identified and resolved
expectations.evidence: Identified in the diagnosis ('Direct contradictions — "be concise" vs "explain your reasoning step by step" vs "write extensive comments explaining each line"') and resolved via a selection principle ('include what changes my next step, drop the rest') plus why-not-what commenting.

expectations.text: Defensive blanket rules (try/catch around every function, 10-line function limit, confirm before every edit) are removed or reframed as judgment-based guidance
expectations.evidence: All three reframed: 'keep functions small enough that each does one clear thing, but don't fragment logic just to hit a line count'; 'Handle errors where something can actually fail ... rather than wrapping everything defensively'; confirmation narrowed to 'destructive or hard-to-reverse actions'.

expectations.text: Rewritten file contains no ALL-CAPS ALWAYS/NEVER/MUST directives (or only for genuine invariants)
expectations.evidence: The fenced rewritten prompt contains zero ALL-CAPS directives; imperatives are lowercase and judgment-scoped ('don't survey options for their own sake', 'Check with me first only for...').

expectations.text: Response includes change notes explaining why the old prescriptive style degrades output on capable models
expectations.evidence: '## What changed and why' section plus an up-front diagnosis: 'this file was written to compensate for a weaker model's failure modes, and on a modern model those compensations actively degrade output'; ALL-CAPS MUSTs 'were written to constrain a weaker model and now suppress judgment.'

claims.claim: Blanket try/catch is the defensive-error-handling anti-pattern that swallows bugs
claims.evidence: Accurate characterization; the rewrite correctly relocates error handling to real failure boundaries (user input, I/O, external calls).

claims.claim: Assumptions were stated in lieu of clarifying questions
claims.evidence: Explicit bulleted assumptions block: original intent inferred, per-edit confirmation treated as a trust guardrail and narrowed, no domain invariants assumed that would justify hard absolutes.

suggestions.reason: All assertions passed for both old and new skill versions. The outputs differ mainly in diagnosis depth and assumption labeling; an assertion requiring that inferred original intents behind each dropped rule be preserved (not just deleted) would better separate careful rewrites from aggressive deletion.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are well-targeted for this eval type but saturated; both versions clear them comfortably.
